consumer: mission::is_complete for MGOAL_FIND_ITEM, which EVALUATES a yes/no: is the required item_count of type->item_id present in the player's crafting_inventory()? — the engine value that drives the 'objective met' state.
scope: items reachable for crafting (carried plus nearby reachable inventory via crafting_inventory()), not only the character's own carried items
decisive_source: src/mission.cpp::mission::is_complete (MGOAL_FIND_ITEM) — builds u.crafting_inventory() and returns whether tmp_inv.has_amount(item_id, item_count) (with a charges fallback), computing the completion predicate itself.
divergence: Required parts sit in a crate on an adjacent reachable tile (in crafting reach) but not in the character's carried inventory: a carried-only has_amount or a raw-items snapshot would answer 'not met' (or mis-tally) while the engine's crafting_inventory predicate returns complete — exposing the wrong scope/authority.
